messages:
Anya: Heads-up: my Go sample app shows a leaked goroutine when I cancel a generator stream with a context timeout.
Anya: Minimal flow: context.WithTimeout -> GenerateStream(ctx, req) -> loop over Recv(); when ctx expires Recv() blocks and never returns.
Micah: Which SDK version? we did some stream refactors recently.
Anya: go-sdk v0.9.3 in the repo.
Sam: We switched to a background reader + token channel. If the reader is stuck on socket.Read, canceling ctx won't wake it unless the transport read is interrupted.
Devon: That explains it. The transport needs to be closed on ctx cancel so the reader gets an IO error and Recv() returns.
Anya: For now I worked around it by spawning a goroutine that waits on ctx.Done() and then calls stream.Close(), but it feels wrong for library users to require that.
Julie: Also observed inconsistent Recv() semantics across examples: sometimes io.EOF on normal finish, sometimes context.Canceled, sometimes a net error. Docs should standardize expected values.
Micah: Proposal: immediate patch to call transport.Close() when ctx is canceled. Long-term: redesign generator API for clearer ergonomics.
Micah: Sketch for iterator-style API that is cancel-friendly:
```
// generator iterator style
type GeneratorIterator interface {
  Next(ctx context.Context) bool // checks ctx each call
  Token() Token
  Err() error // io.EOF for normal end, context.Canceled if canceled
  Close() error // idempotent
}
```
Micah: Then typical loop is:
```
for it.Next(ctx) {
  tok := it.Token()
  // handle tok
}
if errors.Is(it.Err(), context.Canceled) { /* handle cancel */ }
```
Sam: That API separates iteration/cancellation concerns neatly and avoids having Recv() block forever when ctx is done.
Devon: We should also make sure sample apps in quickstart demonstrate the right pattern, so new users don't copy broken code.
Anya: I'll add a small example under dev-examples: a test server that intentionally delays tokens so a short context timeout triggers, and the test asserts no goroutine leak via runtime.NumGoroutine before/after.
Sam: Good. For the interim fix I'll add a small PR to call transport.Close() on ctx cancel. Micah, can you file the issue and include the proposed API in the issue body?
Micah: Yep. I'll open an issue titled "go/sdk: generator stream cancellation and ergonomic iterator API" and push a small patch for transport.Close() now.
ci-bot: Issue created: #2147 by Micah.
Anya: Thanks. Also, can we make Recv()'s error types consistent in the patch so users can reliably compare errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) or io.EOF?
Julie: Agreed. Docs should include a note: "Workaround: if using context timeouts with streaming, either call stream.Close() in a watcher goroutine or use the new iterator API when available."
Devon: Action items summarized: Micah - issue + interim fix; Anya/Devex - sample & test; Julie/Docs - quickstart blurb; Eng - plan iterator API for v0.10.
Sam: Also add a small unit that simulates slow socket behavior and asserts Recv() unblocks after Close/transport.Close. That will prevent regressions.
Anya: I'll PR the sample and test today. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
Micah: Tagging @eng-runtime to prioritize transport change in the sprint planning. :eyes:
